messages:
alex_chang: Heads up — CS flagged a customer with a sharp p95/p99 latency spike starting ~04:10 UTC. They send steady traffic, same model, but tokens/timeouts jumped.

maria_kovacs: seeing the same in metrics. p95 doubled, p99 tripled on node pool A.

jamie_liu: any errors in runtime logs? 5xxs or OOMs?

alex_chang: not 5xx, no oom. traces show lots of cache-miss paths. prefix_kv_cache MISS rate went from ~12% to 78% around 04:08.

sre_bot: incident created: INC-2026-897 (link: https://redwood/incident/INC-2026-897)

tanvi_shah: can you paste the cache metrics? I want eviction rate + size.

alex_chang: metrics snippet:
```
prefix_kv_cache.size 1.2e6
prefix_kv_cache.capacity 1.5e6
prefix_kv_cache.evictions/s 180
prefix_kv_cache.miss_rate 0.78
kv_lookup.latency.p95 320ms -> 610ms
kv_lookup.latency.p99 480ms -> 1.1s
```

maria_kovacs: eviction/s is through the roof. That explains cold KV reads and p99 spikes.

jamie_liu: any recent deploy that changed cache key generation? I'm remembering the model update that switched to dynamic prefix hashing.

alex_chang: good call — there was a minor rollout yesterday that changed prompt normalization: removed trimming of trailing spaces in one code path.

tanvi_shah: if trailing spaces are present in prefixes, cache keys could explode. That fits.

support_tim: customer says payloads look normal. I'll share a sample request body off-thread.

maria_kovacs: quick repro plan: replay customer traffic from 04:00-04:20 in staging with the current runtime. Check miss-rate when normalization flag toggled.

jamie_liu: steps to repro added to INC ticket. rough script:
```
# replay
python tools/replay_trace.py --src s3://traces/customer-123/2026-04-01-04-00.json --target staging --preserve-headers
# monitor
promctl query 'rate(prefix_kv_cache_misses_total[1m])'
```
```
observed: miss_rate jumps to 0.8 on rollout build
```

tanvi_shah: mitigation options:
- roll back normalization change (fast)
- pre-warm cache for hot prefixes (medium)
- increase capacity to reduce evictions (temporary)
- change eviction policy to segmented-LRU to protect hot prefixes (longer)

maria_kovacs: immediate mitigation: rollback to previous build on pool A and increase cache size by 25% as temporary buffer.

alex_chang: I'll trigger rollback on pool A now, and bump cache.size config. Will monitor.

sre_bot: deploy started: rollback runtime build 2026-03-28-9 -> 2026-03-27-5 on pool-A

alex_chang: cache.size bumped from 1.5e6 -> 1.9e6 via /infra/params/prefix_kv_cache/size

jamie_liu: after rollback, miss_rate dropped to ~14% within 3m. p95 back to baseline in 6m.

support_tim: customer confirmed latency back to normal. They saw <10% error rate and p95 within SLA.

tanvi_shah: root cause summary: cache key explosion due to prompt-normalization change that allowed trailing-space variants. High cardinality prefixes caused eviction thrash.

maria_kovacs: follow-ups:
- add normalization unit tests for prefix generation (PR in review: #4521)
- add telemetry to count unique prefixes per minute per model
- implement fast warmup: capture top-100 prefixes and pre-populate KV on deploy
- consider segmented-LRU for hot vs cold sets

jamie_liu: created sub-tasks: #INC-2026-897-1 (rollback verified), -2 (patch normalization), -3 (warmup job), -4 (eviction policy evaluation)

alex_chang: patch landed for trimming: https://git/repo/commit/abc123 — canary tomorrow on 10% traffic

sre_bot: incident resolved: INC-2026-897 resolved — rollback + cache bump successful. postmortem assigned to tanvi_shah

tanvi_shah: draft notes for postmortem:
- timeline
- root cause (cache key bug)
- mitigations (rollback, bump capacity, warmup)
- action items and owners

maria_kovacs: tiny ops note — add a dashboard tile for "unique_prefixes/min" and an alert when it increases > 3x baseline for 5m.

alex_chang: agree. I'll add to dashboards and hook to paging rule with lower severity.

support_tim: customer follow-up scheduled for 06:00 UTC to confirm no recurrence. I'll keep thread updated.

jamie_liu: thanks team. learnings: cache cardinality is a first-class signal. normalization bugs can be high-cost.

alex_chang: leaving logs and replay link in the incident. good job everyone :thumbsup:

sre_bot: NOTE: auto-archive scheduled in 90 days.
